rootCause.explanation: The adapter returned successfully, so its relative guard passed. The outer runner then rejected the same residual using a 24.5-times stricter absolute threshold. The residual is reconstructed by subtracting float64 water depths after a very small source increment and dividing the rounded volume difference by dt, which amplifies representation roundoff.

localSweep.interpretation: The absolute guard is sensitive to sub-millisecond accepted steps and later-state depth magnitudes. Commanded face-volume conservation remains near machine precision. The exact failing dt and residual were not written to the old failure receipt, so their exact values cannot be recovered without a new diagnostic run.

separationFromPriorFailure.globalLongDoubleMassGuard: Did not report a failure before the source-residual guard

implementation: Use one normalized source-residual guard: abs(residual) / max(releaseM3S, 1.0) <= 1e-10 in both adapter and runner.
Add a long-double commanded face-volume residual and keep it as the strict conservation acceptance check.
Keep the float64 state-delta absolute residual as diagnostic telemetry rather than a second stricter stop condition.
Retain the existing long-double global mass-balance guard and all negative-depth, nonfinite, reverse-flow and wet-section fail-closed checks.
targetTests: A small-dt representative state with state-delta residual between the two old thresholds must pass the normalized guard.
A deliberately nonconservative commanded face-volume source must fail.
Zero release must remain an exact no-op.
The six-scenario one-step matrix and the partial-dry-boundary continuation tests must remain passing.
